outside_language: The exact code change: in CefPlatformBrowser.Application.OnBeforeCommandLineProcessing, add commandLine.AppendSwitch("disable-features", "AudioServiceOutOfProcess") after the existing use-mock-keychain line. The member is a protected override in C#; the arch reach vocabulary records it as private.

Cause from the Chromium 156.0.8078.80 sources: IsAudioServiceOutOfProcess() is false under --single-process (content/browser/audio/audio_service.cc 49-54), so the audio service runs in process in a SequenceLocalStorageSlot on the main-thread audio task runner (audio_service.cc 98-108; browser_main_loop.cc 1648-1657). MediaDevicesManager::StartMonitoringAndPopulateCache creates AudioServiceDeviceListener whenever the feature is enabled, without the single-process check (media_devices_manager.cc 878), which binds DeviceNotifier (service.cc 163-171). ~DeviceNotifier calls base::SystemMonitor::Get()->RemoveDevicesChangedObserver (device_notifier.cc). The browser's SystemMonitor belongs to BrowserMainLoop, and the in-process Service is destroyed in BrowserTaskExecutor::Shutdown after BrowserMainLoop, so Get() returns null.

Measured: explicit sinkId runs exit 139 at the symbolized stack SystemMonitor::RemoveDevicesChangedObserver <- DeviceNotifier::~DeviceNotifier <- audio::Service::~Service in stock builds (three runs) and in the proof build; with the switch, the stock build and the proof build exit 0 after the same driver, with the explicit-device stream, device change and speech still working.

Not measured: runs on Apple Silicon, Windows and Linux; long sessions with device hot-plug; any effect of the disabled feature beyond the device-monitoring path and the audio-manager creation check, which single-process already decides.
The separate listening-check question, which is a request to listen, not architecture.
Correction of earlier audio results: media-element leading samples are faded, not lost, and the 8 unaccounted samples of the output-switch run are accounted for.

understanding.purpose: Will you run the 20-second listening check now? You start handoff/macos-completion/validation/listening-check.sh by hand from the repository root. About 4 seconds in you should hear one short quiet tone (0.5 s, 660 Hz), then 2 seconds later the words 'listening check', under 3 seconds of sound in total from the Mac's default output. Afterwards say whether each was heard once, from which speaker, and anything doubled or missing.
